input.title: Powerhouse ships two ready-made analytics processors for DriveOperations and DocumentOperations counters, but Connect no longer enables them by default

input.description: DriveAnalyticsProcessor tracks node adds/copies/moves/updates/deletes on drive documents; DocumentAnalyticsProcessor counts operations on every document type. Both are opt-in.

input.content:
`@powerhousedao/shared/processors/drive-analytics` (re-exported as `@powerhousedao/common/drive-analytics`) exports two processors plus a `processorFactory` that returns both per drive:

- **`DriveAnalyticsProcessor`** — filters to `powerhouse/document-drive` and writes the `DriveOperations` metric, value always `1`, for `ADD_FILE`, `ADD_FOLDER`, `UPDATE_FILE`, `UPDATE_NODE`, `MOVE_NODE`, `COPY_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`. It derives an `actionType` of `CREATED`/`DUPLICATED`/`UPDATED`/`MOVED`/`REMOVED` and a `target` of `NODE` or `DRIVE`.
- **`DocumentAnalyticsProcessor`** — no `documentType` filter at all, so it counts the `DocumentOperations` metric across every document type, tagging `target` as `DRIVE` when the document *is* the drive.

Both are pure counters: `value: 1` per operation, dated by `operation.action.timestampUtcMs` / `operation.timestampUtcMs`, with the aggregation left entirely to query-time granularity and level of detail.

**The "enabled by default" claim is stale.** The draft doc states that Connect enables drive analytics by default through a `ReactorAnalyticsProvider` component in `apps/connect/src/context/reactor-analytics.tsx`. At 6.2.2-dev.45 that component no longer exists, and `apps/connect/src/connect.config.ts` reads:

```typescript
// Analytics off by default; flip to true (or wire a runtime-config field)
// when we want analytics enabled out of the box.
isAnalyticsEnabled: false,
```

Connect's boot path registers processors only from installed packages that export a `processorFactory` — there is no built-in registration of the drive-analytics factory. A `driveAnalyticsEnabled` flag does survive, fed from `PH_CONNECT_DRIVE_ANALYTICS_ENABLED`, alongside `isAnalyticsExternalProcessorsEnabled`. So treat these two processors as a ready-made factory you opt into, not as ambient telemetry you already have.

Provenance: draft `04-Reference/04-Processors/_07-DriveAnalyticsHooks.md` for the metric/dimension design; the enablement correction comes from `packages/shared/processors/drive-analytics/index.ts`, `apps/connect/src/connect.config.ts` and `apps/connect/src/store/reactor.ts` at 6.2.2-dev.45, which contradict the draft.

`@powerhousedao/shared/processors/drive-analytics` (re-exported as `@powerhousedao/common/analytics` -- `packages/common/package.json` maps the `"./analytics"` subpath to `./drive-analytics.ts`, so the internal filename kept the old name but the public subpath did not) exports two processors plus a `processorFactory` that returns both per drive:

- **`DocumentAnalyticsProcessor`** — no `documentType` filter at all, so it counts the `DocumentOperations` metric across every document type, tagging `target` as `DRIVE` when the document *is* the drive.
